definitions.gloss: rotation on its own axis (esp. of a celestial body)
definitions.explanation: In astronomy, the rotation of a body — most often a planet, moon, or star — about its own axis. Distinct from {公転|こうてん}, which refers to revolution around another body. Earth's daily rotation is the canonical example: the Earth's {自転|じてん} produces day and night.

examples.japanese: ⟦{地球|ちきゅう}→地球：03461_chikyuu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{自転|じてん}⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The Earth rotates on its axis.

examples.japanese: {自転|じてん}⟦{周期|しゅうき}→周期：21707_shuuki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{惑星|わくせい}→惑星：05052_wakusei⟧⟦によって→によって：06801_niyotte⟧⟦{大|おお}きく→大きい：00335_ookii⟧⟦{違|ちが}う→違う：01957_chigau⟧。
examples.english: The rotation period varies greatly from planet to planet.
We have day and night because the Earth rotates on its axis.

examples.japanese: ⟦{金星|きんせい}→金星：15896_kinsei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{他|ほか}→他：04129_hoka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{惑星|わくせい}→惑星：05052_wakusei⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{逆方向|ぎゃくほうこう}→逆方向：15966_gyakuhoukou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{自転|じてん}⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧おり、{自転|じてん}⟦{周期|しゅうき}→周期：21707_shuuki⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{非常|ひじょう}→非常：01598_hijou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{遅|おそ}い→遅い：00533_osoi⟧。
examples.english: Venus rotates in the opposite direction from the other planets, and its rotation period is extremely slow.

notes:
{自転|じてん} is the standard astronomical term for a body's rotation about its own axis. It is paired with ⟦{公転|こうてん}→公転：27359_kouten⟧ ("orbital revolution"), and the contrast between the two is one of the first things taught in Japanese science classes when planetary motion is introduced.

FORMS:
- {自|じ} ("self, on one's own") + {転|てん} ("turn, rotate") → {自転|じてん}

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自転|じてん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to rotate (on its axis)
- {自転|じてん}⟦{周期|しゅうき}→周期：21707_shuuki⟧: rotation period
- {自転|じてん}⟦{軸|じく}→軸：14304_jiku⟧: axis of rotation
- {自転|じてん}⟦{速度|そくど}→速度：03319_sokudo⟧: rotation speed
- ⟦{地球|ちきゅう}→地球：03461_chikyuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{自転|じてん}: the Earth's rotation
- {自転|じてん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{公転|こうてん}→公転：27359_kouten⟧: rotation and revolution

CONTRAST WITH {公転|こうてん}:
- {自転|じてん}: rotation on its own axis (e.g., Earth turns once every ~24 hours)
- ⟦{公転|こうてん}→公転：27359_kouten⟧: revolution around another body (e.g., Earth orbits the Sun once a year)
- These are typically taught and used as a pair in introductory astronomy.

SIMILAR / RELATED TERMS:
- ⟦{回転|かいてん}→回転：00141_kaiten⟧: rotation, spinning (general term, not limited to celestial bodies — wheels, motors, dancers)
- ⟦スピン→スピン：27365_supin⟧: spin (loanword; common in everyday and physics contexts, e.g., a figure-skating spin or particle spin)
- {歳差|さいさ}⟦{運動|うんどう}→運動：00821_undou⟧: precession (the slow wobble of a rotation axis)

USAGE:
- For non-astronomical "rotation," use ⟦{回転|かいてん}→回転：00141_kaiten⟧: ⟦タイヤ→タイヤ：06330_taiya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{回転|かいてん}→回転：00141_kaiten⟧ ("the rotation of the tires"), ⟦モーター→モーター：23127_mootaa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{回転|かいてん}→回転：00141_kaiten⟧⟦{数|すう}→数：03360_suu⟧ ("the motor's RPM"). {自転|じてん} sounds odd for everyday objects.
- {自転|じてん} is also part of the everyday word ⟦{自転車|じてんしゃ}→自転車：00633_jitensha⟧ ("bicycle"), where the meaning is more like "self-turning vehicle."
- Beware homophones: ⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧ ("dictionary"), ⟦{事典|じてん}→事典：21891_jiten⟧ ("encyclopedia / reference work"), and ⟦{時点|じてん}→時点：12970_jiten⟧ ("point in time") all share the reading じてん but use entirely different kanji.
